title: Deduplication Check Lacking Single-Write Atomicity (Read-Then-Write TOCTOU)
pattern: Checking if a unique network message or transaction ID has been processed, and then executing a state-modifying action and recording the message ID as "processed" in separate, non-atomic database steps.
why_bad: Under concurrent execution (e.g., multiple workers processing from a shared partition), duplicate messages can be processed simultaneously [16]. Because the read check and write record are separate operations, both threads can execute step 1 before either writes the ID in step 3. Both threads will conclude the message is new and execute the non-idempotent side-effect, causing double processing [16].
detection: Identify message handlers containing a read query on a transaction/message ID followed by write queries to a database, where the read and write operations are not performed atomically under an exclusive database lock, a unique primary key constraint write, or a SQL transaction.
fix: Enforce atomic check-and-write semantics. For example, insert the unique message ID into a dedicated table with a `UNIQUE` primary key constraint as the very first step, proceeding only if the insertion succeeds, or perform the check and update within a serialized transaction [48, 49, 133].
source: Alex Petrov, *Database Internals*, Concurrency Control / passages [15, 16, 48, 49]; Martin Kleppmann, *Designing Data-Intensive Applications*, Chapter 7 / passage [133].
